issues.description: The UML diagram in the problem statement labels the class as 'Course' while the rest of the exercise (narrative, template, and solution) consistently refer to the class as 'Lecture'. This naming mismatch in the problem statement can confuse students about the intended class name and where to add attributes/methods.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the UML class label from 'Course' to 'Lecture' in the problem statement so it matches the class name used in the template and solution (or alternatively update the template/solution to use 'Course' consistently). Ensure the UML's attributes and method signatures remain unchanged.

issues.description: The problem text and code refer to a Lecture class and its attributes, but the UML embedded in the problem statement names the class as Course. This inconsistent identifier for the same conceptual entity (Lecture vs. Course) can confuse students when mapping the textual requirements to the UML and the provided Lecture.java template/solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the UML class in the problem statement from Course to Lecture so the UML, textual description, template, and solution use the same class name (Lecture). Alternatively, if Course is intended, update template and solution to use Course consistently; preferred fix is to change the UML to Lecture to match the exercise wording and files.
